sql:
-- Let me verify one of these cases. 
-- Match 980942: match_winner=13, player on team 2 (RCB), scored 100 runs. Team 2 != 13, so team 2 lost. Correct!
-- Match 734054: match_winner=1, player on team 4 (KXIP), scored 115 runs. Team 4 != 1, so team 4 lost. Correct!

-- The query is working correctly. Let me now submit the final result with all player names.
SELECT DISTINCT p.player_name
FROM batsman_scored bbb
JOIN ball_by_ball bbb2 ON bbb.match_id = bbb2.match_id 
    AND bbb.over_id = bbb2.over_id 
    AND bbb.ball_id = bbb2.ball_id 
    AND bbb.innings_no = bbb2.innings_no
JOIN player p ON bbb2.striker = p.player_id
JOIN match m ON bbb.match_id = m.match_id
JOIN player_match pm ON bbb.match_id = pm.match_id AND bbb2.striker = pm.player_id
WHERE pm.team_id != m.match_winner
GROUP BY bbb2.striker, p.player_name
HAVING SUM(bbb.runs_scored) >= 100
ORDER BY p.player_name;
